variants.title: Build a reproducible corpus
variants.context: Turning raw sources into a reproducible corpus is four steps. Acquire captures source, license, consent or policy basis, retrieval time, and an immutable raw reference. Normalize extracts fields, standardizes encoding and language, and keeps a stable example ID. Filter removes unwanted formats, personal data, unsafe material, spam, boilerplate, and duplicates with recorded rules. Freeze creates split manifests, statistics, and versioned code and thresholds.
variants.prompt: A team is assembling a pretraining corpus from a public web archive for the first time. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Freeze the split manifests, compute statistics, and version the code and thresholds that produced the snapshot.
Capture the source, license, policy basis, retrieval time, and an immutable reference to each raw archive file.
Extract the useful text, standardize encoding and language, and attach a stable example ID with its provenance.
Remove unwanted formats, personal data, unsafe material, spam, boilerplate, and duplicates under recorded rules.

variants.hint: Which step has to happen while the raw bytes are still untouched?
variants.explanation: Acquire, normalize, filter, freeze. Rights and retrieval evidence cannot be reconstructed after the text has been extracted and cleaned.

variants.title: Build a reproducible corpus
variants.context: Turning raw sources into a reproducible corpus is four steps. Acquire captures source, license, consent or policy basis, retrieval time, and an immutable raw reference. Normalize extracts fields, standardizes encoding and language, and keeps a stable example ID. Filter removes unwanted formats, personal data, unsafe material, spam, boilerplate, and duplicates with recorded rules. Freeze creates split manifests, statistics, and versioned code and thresholds.
variants.prompt: A question-and-answer community is added as a new source alongside the existing crawl. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Recompute the manifests and statistics so the snapshot including this source is reproducible.
Parse posts and accepted answers into examples with stable IDs that point back to their thread.
Record the community's license, item-level policy, and the retrieval time of the export.
Apply quality signals and remove credentials, personal data, and content the item-level policy excludes.

variants.hint: Quality signals such as accepted answers are filters, not proof of permission.
variants.explanation: Every source passes through the same four steps, because an unversioned addition makes the whole snapshot unreproducible.

variants.title: Build a reproducible corpus
variants.context: Turning raw sources into a reproducible corpus is four steps. Acquire captures source, license, consent or policy basis, retrieval time, and an immutable raw reference. Normalize extracts fields, standardizes encoding and language, and keeps a stable example ID. Filter removes unwanted formats, personal data, unsafe material, spam, boilerplate, and duplicates with recorded rules. Freeze creates split manifests, statistics, and versioned code and thresholds.
variants.prompt: A filter threshold is loosened and the corpus must be rebuilt from the same archives. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Apply the new threshold and record it as the rule that produced this pass.
Re-run extraction and normalization to regenerate examples with their original stable IDs.
Resolve the immutable raw references the previous snapshot recorded so the same bytes are read again.
Publish a new frozen snapshot with updated manifests, statistics, and versioned thresholds.

variants.hint: A changed threshold produces a different dataset, not an edit of the old one.
variants.explanation: Because raw references and thresholds were versioned, the rebuild is reproducible and the two snapshots can be compared.

variants.title: Protect the evaluation boundary
variants.context: A leakage-resistant evaluation boundary starts from raw examples with stable IDs, timestamps, origin, and the entity or document family each belongs to. Duplicates are clustered so each group lands in one partition, the test manifest is frozen and access-limited, and only the training and validation partitions are used to fit models and choose changes.
variants.prompt: A document classifier is trained on filings that often come in near-identical families. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Assign each cluster to exactly one partition and freeze the test manifest with limited access.
Store each example with a stable ID, timestamp, origin, and the document family it belongs to.
Fit models and choose changes using only the training and validation partitions.
Cluster exact and near duplicates so an entire family is treated as one unit.

variants.hint: The unit that can leak is not always a single row.
variants.explanation: Grouping before splitting is what makes the held-out score a claim about unseen documents rather than about paraphrases of seen ones.

variants.title: Protect the evaluation boundary
variants.context: A leakage-resistant evaluation boundary starts from raw examples with stable IDs, timestamps, origin, and the entity or document family each belongs to. Duplicates are clustered so each group lands in one partition, the test manifest is frozen and access-limited, and only the training and validation partitions are used to fit models and choose changes.
variants.prompt: A benchmark's prompts may already exist somewhere in a large crawl. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Freeze the benchmark as a held-out manifest and document the removal procedure that was run.
Train and validate on the cleaned candidates only.
Search the training candidates for those prompts, their answers, and close variants, then remove the matches.
Identify the benchmark items with stable IDs so they can be searched for by content, not only by file.

variants.hint: Exact file hashes are not the only way a benchmark item can appear.
variants.explanation: Benchmark leakage is checked by content across sources, and the removal procedure is documented so the score can be interpreted later.

variants.title: Protect the evaluation boundary
variants.context: A leakage-resistant evaluation boundary starts from raw examples with stable IDs, timestamps, origin, and the entity or document family each belongs to. Duplicates are clustered so each group lands in one partition, the test manifest is frozen and access-limited, and only the training and validation partitions are used to fit models and choose changes.
variants.prompt: One merchant appears in thousands of rows and the model must generalize to merchants it has never seen. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Group all of a merchant's rows, including near-duplicate transactions, into a single unit.
Develop against training and validation only, leaving the frozen test partition untouched.
Attach the merchant identifier to every example as the entity the split must respect.
Send each merchant to exactly one of train, validation, and test, then freeze the test manifest.

variants.hint: What does the deployment question say the model has never seen?
variants.explanation: The split unit comes from the deployment claim. Splitting merchant rows at random would measure memorization of known merchants.

variants.title: Name the contamination
variants.context: Contamination has several distinct forms. Entity leakage repeats one user, patient, merchant, or document family across splits. Temporal leakage trains on information from after the prediction or benchmark cutoff. Benchmark leakage puts evaluation prompts, answers, or close variants into training candidates. Process leakage lets repeated tuning against final test results turn the test set into validation data.
variants.prompt: Match each contamination type to what it describes.

pairs.label: Entity leakage
pairs.detail: One user, patient, merchant, conversation, or document family appears on both sides of the split.

pairs.label: Temporal leakage
pairs.detail: Training uses information from after the prediction or benchmark cutoff.

pairs.label: Benchmark leakage
pairs.detail: Evaluation prompts, answers, or close variants are present in the training candidates.

pairs.label: Process leakage
pairs.detail: Repeated tuning against final test results turns the held-out set into validation data.

variants.hint: One of these needs no data movement at all to happen.
variants.explanation: The four types need different controls, so a single deduplication pass cannot address all of them.

variants.title: Name the contamination
variants.context: Contamination has several distinct forms. Entity leakage repeats one user, patient, merchant, or document family across splits. Temporal leakage trains on information from after the prediction or benchmark cutoff. Benchmark leakage puts evaluation prompts, answers, or close variants into training candidates. Process leakage lets repeated tuning against final test results turn the test set into validation data.
variants.prompt: A review of a candidate corpus produces four findings. Match each finding to the contamination type it represents.

pairs.label: The same patient's earlier and later visits sit in train and test
Articles published after the forecast cutoff were included in training
A paraphrase of a held-out evaluation question is in a scraped forum thread
The team has compared 40 model variants on the final test set this quarter

variants.hint: Ask what the evaluation score would still be allowed to claim.
variants.explanation: Naming the type points at the control: group the split, enforce the cutoff, screen by content, or restrict access to the test results.

variants.title: Name the contamination
variants.context: Contamination has several distinct forms. Entity leakage repeats one user, patient, merchant, or document family across splits. Temporal leakage trains on information from after the prediction or benchmark cutoff. Benchmark leakage puts evaluation prompts, answers, or close variants into training candidates. Process leakage lets repeated tuning against final test results turn the test set into validation data.
variants.prompt: A second review produces four findings. Match each finding to the contamination type it represents.

pairs.label: A conversation was chunked and its parts were split at random across partitions
A feature is built from a table that is only populated after the outcome is known
A public copy of the benchmark answer key was crawled into the training candidates
Test-set error analysis is used every week to pick the next feature to build

variants.hint: Chunking does not change which unit is allowed to leak.
variants.explanation: Splitting derived pieces of one unit at random reintroduces entity leakage even when every individual row looks distinct.

variants.title: Decide how to use a source
variants.context: Sources are chosen for the unique signal they add, the rights that can be established, and the error modes they introduce. Public availability is not permission, deduplication has to run across sources rather than only within each one, and synthetic data must stay distinguishable from real data and be judged on independently collected real examples.
variants.prompt: A large forum's posts are freely downloadable and a team wants to train on them. What must happen before they are used?
options: Remove usernames from the posts, which resolves the rights question for public text.
Record the use restrictions, personal-data handling, opt-out obligations, and who approved the source.
Confirm the posts are downloadable without authentication, which establishes permitted use.
optionFeedback: Stripping usernames is one privacy control, and it does not create a lawful basis or a permitted use.
Correct: documentation must record permitted use and approval, because availability is not permission.
Reachability says nothing about license, consent, or the obligations attached to the content.
variants.hint: What does the dataset documentation have to be able to show later?
variants.explanation: Public availability is not permission to train. Restrictions, opt-out obligations, and an approver belong in the documentation.

variants.title: Decide how to use a source
variants.context: Sources are chosen for the unique signal they add, the rights that can be established, and the error modes they introduce. Public availability is not permission, deduplication has to run across sources rather than only within each one, and synthetic data must stay distinguishable from real data and be judged on independently collected real examples.
variants.prompt: The same press release turns up in the crawl, in a forum thread quoting it, and in a repository's documentation. Each source was deduplicated internally. What control is missing?
options: Deduplication across sources, since a copied document can appear in several of them.
A larger crawl sample, so the repeated document carries less relative weight.
A stricter boilerplate filter, since press releases are formulaic text.
optionFeedback: Correct: within-source deduplication cannot see a copy that lives in a different source.
Adding data does not remove the duplicate, and the copies still concentrate on the same content.
A boilerplate rule targets a text style and would still miss copies of ordinary documents.
variants.hint: Where does a copied document hide from a within-source pass?
variants.explanation: Deduplicate across sources, not only within each one, and keep provenance fields so the copies remain auditable.

variants.title: Decide how to use a source
variants.context: Sources are chosen for the unique signal they add, the rights that can be established, and the error modes they introduce. Public availability is not permission, deduplication has to run across sources rather than only within each one, and synthetic data must stay distinguishable from real data and be judged on independently collected real examples.
variants.prompt: Synthetic examples are generated to cover a rare failure mode that real data barely contains. How should they be handled?
options: Mix them into the real examples so the model cannot learn to treat them differently.
Evaluate them on a held-out sample of the synthetic data covering the same rare mode.
Keep them distinguishable from real data and judge them on independently collected real examples.
optionFeedback: Losing the provenance flag makes the synthetic share impossible to audit or remove later.
A synthetic holdout measures how well the generator was imitated, not whether real performance improved.
Correct: the provenance flag preserves auditability and the real holdout is what shows a genuine gain.
variants.hint: What evidence would show the synthetic data actually helped?
variants.explanation: Synthetic data can fill rare scenarios, but it must stay labeled as synthetic and be validated on independently collected real examples.

variants.title: Do the mixture math
variants.context: Dataset mixing is the weighted combination of source streams during training over a fixed 100 percent budget. A source's raw size does not have to equal its training weight: smaller trusted material is often sampled more often when it supplies a capability a large noisy source lacks.
variants.prompt: A curated reference corpus is 2 percent of the raw token pool but receives 12 percent of the training budget. By what factor is it upsampled relative to its raw share?
variants.hint: Compare the training weight with the raw share, not with the other sources.
variants.explanation: A source's raw size does not have to equal its weight, and the ratio between them states how strongly it was upsampled.

mistakes.feedback: Subtracted the raw share from the weight instead of taking the ratio.
Reported the training weight rather than the factor above the raw share.

variants.title: Do the mixture math
variants.context: Dataset mixing is the weighted combination of source streams during training over a fixed 100 percent budget. A source's raw size does not have to equal its training weight: smaller trusted material is often sampled more often when it supplies a capability a large noisy source lacks.
variants.prompt: A mixture allocates 45 percent to a web crawl, 25 percent to curated reference material, and 20 percent to code. The rest goes to synthetic data. What percentage is synthetic?
variants.hint: The training budget is fixed at 100 percent.
variants.explanation: Mixture weights are an allocation of one fixed budget, so raising any source's weight has to lower another's.

mistakes.feedback: Reported the total already allocated rather than what remains.
Subtracted only the web crawl from the budget and ignored the other two sources.

variants.title: Do the mixture math
variants.context: Dataset mixing is the weighted combination of source streams during training over a fixed 100 percent budget. A source's raw size does not have to equal its training weight: smaller trusted material is often sampled more often when it supplies a capability a large noisy source lacks.
variants.prompt: A noisy crawl makes up 60 percent of the raw token pool but is given 30 percent of the training budget. By what factor is it downweighted relative to its raw share?
variants.hint: The same comparison works in both directions.
variants.explanation: Downweighting a large noisy source is the other half of the same decision that upsamples a small trusted one.

mistakes.feedback: Reported the training weight rather than the factor below the raw share.
Divided the weight by the raw share, which gives the reciprocal of the downweighting factor.
